prerequisites: Knowledge of mathematics, especially differential and integral calculus and linear algebra

learning_outcomes.text: The graduates know the connections between discrete and continuous system descriptions.
The graduates have in-depth knowledge of the representation forms of continuous and discrete signals and the transmission behavior of systems.

The graduates are able to abstract and formally represent the behavior of components from the sub-areas of mechatronics. They can mathematically analyze the interactions in a mechatronic system across disciplines.

syllabus_topics: System representations in the time domain
Application of Laplace transformation in system theory
Application of Fourier transformation in system theory (discrete and continuous)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either a written exam or an oral exam, chosen by the lecturer. The duration for the oral exam is specified in the general part of the examination regulations, and for the written exam in the currently valid study regulations. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 8 experiments.
